subject: Subprocessor authorization, export restrictions, and temporary escape-hatch inquiry
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finrise.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: legal.ops@finrise.com
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Subprocessor export classification and emergency access paths

Jonas,

Quick one from our security & legal teams: as part of an audit ahead of our EU expansion, we need a granular breakdown of any subprocessors that may process FinRise customer data and whether any of them are classified as temporary/standby partners outside the EU. Specifically:

- Full inventory (name, country, role, SCCs/international transfer mechanism if applicable)
- Which subprocessors are provisioned only for short-term/load-shedding events (and how long the access is retained)
- Whether Redwood has an operational "escape-hatch" to revoke access and an evidence package for revocation within 24 hours

Can you provide a bundle for us by EOD tomorrow? If there's anything that requires procurement/legal redlines, please call it out.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Infrastructure Security
FinRise Payments

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finrise.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor export classification and emergency access paths

Liam —

Thanks for the clear ask. We'll assemble a compliance bundle and a short operational runbook describing our revocation path. A couple quick clarifications to ensure we give exactly what you need:

1) For the inventory CSV, do you need encryption-at-rest and key-ownership fields (KMS/HSM owner)? We can include key IDs and KMS provider if that helps your Security team.
2) For temporary partners: do you want durations (e.g., "used <72 hours") or the provisioning trigger (manual on-call escalation vs. automated failover)?

Plan: Kimberly will attach the inventory + topology PDF. I'll draft a 24-hour revocation plan and Naomi will prepare the DPA addendum (signable). If acceptable, we'll share the Drive link + DocuSign envelope.

Putting a holder in your calendar for a short 30-minute sync if you want to walk through.

Jonas Weber
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Subprocessor inventory (initial drop)

Attached is the initial inventory CSV and a topology map. High-level notes inline:

- EdgeFlow CDN (edgeflow-eu-temp) — operated in DE, deployed as a short-term regional edge for emergency traffic spillover. Access is provisioned by runtime-team for up to 7 days unless extended. No persistent storage of raw PII; logs retained 30 days for troubleshooting. [Attachment: subprocessor_inventory.csv (CSV, 42KB)]
- CacheWave Observability — EU region, metrics-only, retained 90 days, supports controlled read-only telemetry export to US for platform analytics. [Attachment: redwood_subproc_map.pdf (PDF, 320KB)]
- VaultGuard KMS — multi-region KMS managed by Redwood; key material held in HSMs in the EU for EU-bound customers where required.

Temporary/standby processors are tagged in the CSV under column "provisioning_model". For each temporary entry we've included the provisioning trigger and TTL. Rishi: flagging a known exception where EdgeFlow requested S3-style log forwarding to a US bucket during a 2026-06 incident — that is documented in the incident packet and requires the FinRise sign-off if you want to forbid that pattern.

Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Vendor Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: legal.ops@finrise.com <legal.ops@finrise.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor authorization, export restrictions, and temporary escape-hatch inquiry

Team,

Thanks for the files. A couple of legal items we need to resolve before approving production-scope access for FinRise EU customers:

- A signable attestation that temporary subprocessors (tagged "temporary" in your CSV) will have access revoked within 24 hours of our request and that any exported logs will be deleted within 72 hours unless expressly retained by mutual agreement.
- Confirmation that any cross-border transfers used for incident response will be pre-approved only with explicit customer consent or an approved legal exception. The prior incident you flagged (June 2026) is a material concern; we need the exact retention evidence and the export destination for that event.

Please provide the attestation as a DocuSign or similar signable addendum and the incident evidence. We also want the contact information for the on-call operations lead who can accept a revocation request 24/7.

Regards,
FinRise Legal Ops

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Legal Ops <legal.ops@finrise.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finrise.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor authorization, export restrictions, and temporary escape-hatch inquiry

Legal Ops —

Appreciate the specifics. Actions below (we've linked artifacts in Drive and attached a signable addendum):

- Attestation addendum: uploaded a signable PDF to DocuSign (link: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-redwood-finrise) and attached DPA_addendum_redwood_signable.pdf. The addendum commits to revocation within 24 hours and deletion of exported logs within 72 hours unless a documented exception is in place.
- Incident evidence: in Drive we dropped the June 2026 incident packet (folder: /redwood/finrise-subproc-evidence/incident-2026-06). It includes the export destination (s3://redwood-incident-exports/us-east-1/finrise-incident-20260611), retention logs, and the ticket timeline.
- Operational runbook: short playbook outlining the on-call revocation path is in the Drive folder; the 24/7 contact is our on-call infra lead: Rishi Malhotra (rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, +1-415-555-0134). Rishi is CC'd here.

If you'd like, we'll schedule a 30-minute bridge to walk through the evidence and the DocuSign flow. If Legal signs the addendum we can then mark the FinRise account with an enforced transfer block for any temporary subprocessor unless we mutually agree.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DPA_addendum_redwood_signable.pdf (PDF, 88KB)]
